support_spans: delta wave present in QRS complex B
concepts.why: The patient's ECG shows alternating QRS complex morphologies and a delta wave, which are characteristic of Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome.
The patient has mild wheezing, which could be a sign of pulmonary hypertension, but the chest radiograph shows no acute cardiopulmonary processes.
The patient has a history of polysubstance abuse and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, which could be related to cardiomyopathy due to substance abuse.

support_spans: bilateral scrotal and lower extremity edema for 10 days
concepts.why: The patient has bilateral scrotal and lower extremity edema, which could be a sign of nephrotic syndrome.
It explains the global hypokinesis, elevated troponin, and high brain natriuretic peptide levels found in the patient.
It could explain the absence of acute cardiopulmonary processes on the chest radiograph despite symptoms of heart failure.
